documents.title: Follow-up Visit - Hypertension
documents.author: PCP

S: Brought home log (new cuff): mostly 145-155/88-96 over the last month. Taking lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, HCTZ 25 and KCl every day. Salt intake moderate. No headache, chest pain, dyspnea or vision change. Lupus quiet, prednisone 10.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Emergency department physician note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Hospital ED, seen Sunday 04/05/2026 11:50.

CC: weak, dark urine, spots on legs.

HPI: 49F with SLE (hydroxychloroquine, prednisone 10 mg), asplenia since 2023, primary CNS lymphoma in remission. Three days of generalized weakness, urine the color of tea, and a new rash of tiny red-purple dots on both lower legs. Started on hydralazine about three weeks ago for blood pressure.

Meds: hydralazine 25 mg TID (new), lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, HCTZ 25, KCl 20 mEq, hydroxychloroquine 200 bid, prednisone 10, cholecalciferol, calcium carbonate.
Allergy: sulfonamides.

Vitals: T 37.8 C, BP 150/90, HR 110, RR 20.
Exam: tired, jaundiced, scleral icterus. Petechiae over both lower legs. Abdomen soft, healed LUQ scar. Heart tachycardic, regular. Lungs clear. Neuro nonfocal.

Labs: Hgb 8.0, platelets 40, LDH 700, total bilirubin 3.2 (direct 0.8), haptoglobin <10. Smear: schistocytes present. Creatinine 0.9. DAT negative.

MDM: hemolysis with schistocytes and thrombocytopenia, low-grade temperature, tachycardia. TTP must be excluded; recent hydralazine is a candidate drug cause. Hydralazine held. ADAMTS13 sent. Hematology consulted from the ED. Asplenic with temperature 37.8: cultures drawn, observed closely.

Disposition: admitted to medicine, telemetry.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admitted 04/05/2026. Discharged 04/09/2026.

Diagnoses: drug-induced hemolytic anemia with thrombocytopenia, attributed to hydralazine. SLE, hypertension, asplenia, history of primary CNS lymphoma.

Course: presented with weakness, dark urine and lower-leg petechiae three weeks after starting hydralazine. Hgb 8.0, platelets 40, LDH 700, indirect hyperbilirubinemia, haptoglobin undetectable, schistocytes on smear. DAT negative. Creatinine normal throughout. Hematology saw her on arrival; with a rapid ADAMTS13 activity of 64% resulting on day 2, TTP was excluded and plasma exchange was not started. Hydralazine was stopped on admission and not restarted. Blood cultures no growth. No transfusion required. Hemolysis markers and platelets improved daily: at discharge Hgb 8.7, platelets 96, LDH 430, total bilirubin 1.7. Prednisone continued at her usual 10 mg.

NEW ALLERGY: hydralazine (drug-induced hemolysis). Do not rechallenge.

Discharge medications: STOP hydralazine. Continue lisinopril 20, amlodipine 5, hydrochlorothiazide 25, potassium chloride 20 mEq, hydroxychloroquine 200 mg bid, prednisone 10 mg, cholecalciferol, calcium carbonate.

Follow-up: PCP within one week with CBC, LDH and bilirubin. Hematology as needed. Blood pressure regimen to be adjusted by PCP.

Hospital Medicine

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Spoke with pt day after discharge. Tired, urine lighter, legs still spotty. No fever. Has stopped hydralazine and threw the bottle out. Hydralazine added to allergy list in our chart. Appt Monday 4/13 with labs.

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Admission 4/5-4/9 reviewed: hemolytic anemia with schistocytes and plt 40 three weeks after I started hydralazine; ADAMTS13 64%, DAT neg, attributed to hydralazine, which is stopped and now on her allergy list.

Feels better each day, energy coming back. Urine normal color. Leg spots fading. No fever, no bleeding.

Exam: BP 146/92. Mild residual scleral icterus. Scattered fading purpuric spots on both shins. Heart regular. Lungs clear.

Labs today: Hgb 10.4, platelets 168, LDH 300, bilirubin 1.1 - all moving the right way.

A/P:
1. Drug-induced hemolytic anemia + thrombocytopenia - resolving off hydralazine. Repeat labs 4 wks.
2. HTN still above goal without hydralazine - increase amlodipine to 10 mg. Continue lisinopril, HCTZ, KCl. Home log.
3. SLE - stable on HCQ + pred 10.
RTC 4 weeks.

documents.title: Home BP
documents.author: patient
documents.body: BPs since the amlodipine went up: 134/84, 130/82, 136/86, 128/80, 132/84. Is that ok?

documents.title: RE: Home BP
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Those numbers are right where they should be. Keep the same dose. See you on the 11th.

conditions.label: Senile purpura
conditions.note: nonpalpable purpura of the shins with normal platelets, long-term prednisone

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Back to normal energy. No dark urine. Some purple marks on her shins haven't gone away and new ones show up after she bumps her legs on the desk at work. Home BP 128-136/80-86 on amlodipine 10.

O: BP as charted. No icterus. Shins: several flat, nonpalpable purple patches of varying age on thin, shiny skin; no petechiae. No edema.

Labs today: Hgb 12.1, platelets 230, LDH 196, haptoglobin 92, bilirubin 0.6. BMP normal.

A/P:
1. Hydralazine-induced hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia - resolved. Allergy listed.
2. Purple patches on shins with normal platelets now, fragile skin after 15 years of prednisone - senile (steroid) purpura. Benign. Protect shins, no treatment needed.
3. HTN - at goal on amlodipine 10, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25. Continue KCl.
4. SLE quiet. History of PCNSL - MRI July.
Physical in September.

documents.title: Refill

documents.body: Done - KCl 20 mEq and amlodipine 10 mg sent for 90 days with refills. The old 5 mg prescription was cancelled at the pharmacy.
